claims.text: An HTTP/1.1 request consists of a start line (method, request-target, version), zero or more header fields, an empty line, and an optional body.
An HTTP/1.1 response consists of a status line (version, status code, reason phrase), header fields, an empty line, and an optional body.
Lines in an HTTP/1.1 message are terminated by CRLF (\r\n).
An HTTP/1.1 client must send exactly one Host header field in a request; a server must respond 400 to a request lacking it.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9112 §3.2 Request Target / Host; RFC 9110 §7.2 Host

claims.text: Content-Length gives the size of the message body in bytes (octets) and a recipient uses it to determine where the body ends.
A 204 No Content response does not include a message body.
A 304 Not Modified response indicates the client may reuse its stored representation.
A GET request normally has no body (a body on GET has no defined semantics).
The output shown for scripts/http/raw-request.sh at stage-0 (status line, seven headers including Server: Caddy, blank line, HTML) is what the stage-0 Compose stack returns.
Reading the raw request/response by hand is the fastest way to locate whether a problem is in the client, server or network.
claims.source_hint: author's recommendation; condition: when the failure is reproducible with one request
